gap: No result ChatGPT got states what going wireless costs in measured latency on an under-$100 magnetic board: HLPlanet measured the Gamakay TK75 TMR at 0.60 ms wired and 0.75 ms on 2.4 GHz, so the dongle adds 0.15 ms, and the wired figure is 4.8 times the 0.125 ms report interval those pages quote for 8,000 Hz.
standout_why: Compared against mechanicalkeyboard.net (best-budget list), mkbguide.com (under-$100 list), gamepadsquire.com, setupinsider.com and the hlplanet.com list page. mkbguide and mechanicalkeyboard.net already give the report intervals (0.125 ms at 8,000 Hz, 1 ms at 1,000 Hz, 8 ms at 125 Hz), and both say these are not latency. Gamepadsquire gives battery sizes and one runtime (FUN60 Ultra, about 3 hours at 8K wireless with RGB on). The hlplanet list page gives measured latency for other boards (ATK RS6 0.16 ms, Glorious GMMK 3 HE 5.3 ms). In my reads, none of them gave a wired and a 2.4 GHz measurement for the same under-$100 board, the difference between them, or measured latency set against the report interval. The two measurements come from HLPlanet's separate TK75 TMR review, which was not among ChatGPT's results. I read the hlplanet list page through a summary, so its full table may carry the TK75 TMR row.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the overall pick: a cheaper wired 8,000 Hz board still wins on price. It does decide the wireless segment. The Gamakay TK75 TMR is the only candidate here with a named reviewer's wired and 2.4 GHz measurements, and its measured 2.4 GHz total (0.75 ms) is shorter than the 1 ms report interval of a board that drops to 1,000 Hz on its dongle (AULA F75 HE, per Gamepadsquire). It also puts a number on ChatGPT's own caveat that 8K polling is not latency. The TK75 TMR is under $100 only at the sale price, by $10.01, and Gamakay's sale ends 2026-11-30.

findings.label: Measured latency, wired and 2.4 GHz (HLPlanet)
findings.value: 0.60 ms wired, 0.75 ms on 2.4 GHz; Bluetooth not tested
findings.source_title: HLPlanet Gamakay TK75 TMR review (Marcus Richardson, 2026-05-18)
findings.note: HLPlanet's OSLTT method: time from physical keycap contact to signal receipt by the computer. The same review lists 8,000 Hz wired and 2.4 GHz, 1,000 Hz Bluetooth, 8,000 mAh, about 1,100 g, and a price of $119.99 at review.

findings.label: Latency added by going wireless (derived)
findings.source_title: HLPlanet Gamakay TK75 TMR review (Marcus Richardson, 2026-05-18)
findings.note: 0.75 ms − 0.60 ms = 0.15 ms; 0.15 ÷ 0.60 = 25%. Both inputs are HLPlanet's measurements.

findings.label: Measured wired latency against the 8,000 Hz report interval (derived)
findings.source_title: HLPlanet Gamakay TK75 TMR review (Marcus Richardson, 2026-05-18)
findings.note: 1,000 ms ÷ 8,000 Hz = 0.125 ms per report; 0.60 ÷ 0.125 = 4.8; 0.75 ÷ 0.125 = 6. The 0.125 ms figure rival pages quote is about a fifth of the measured wired total on this board.

findings.label: 1,000 Hz wireless report interval against the TK75 TMR's measured 2.4 GHz total (derived)
findings.value: 1 ms between reports at 1,000 Hz, against 0.75 ms measured in total
findings.source_title: Gamepadsquire: Best Budget Hall Effect Keyboards Under $100 in 2026
findings.note: Gamepadsquire lists the AULA F75 HE at 8,000 Hz wired and 1,000 Hz on 2.4 GHz. 1,000 ms ÷ 1,000 Hz = 1 ms between reports, longer than the 0.75 ms HLPlanet measured end to end on the TK75 TMR's 2.4 GHz link. A report interval is a floor on worst-case delay, not a latency measurement.

findings.label: Maker's '0.06 ms' latency claim against its own 8 kHz report interval (derived)
findings.value: 0.06 ms claimed is 0.48 of one 0.125 ms report interval
findings.source_title: Gamakay TK75HE V2 Hall Effect keyboard 8K Polling Rate 0.005mm RT Accuracy
findings.note: Store text read through gamakay.com's search: 'Ultra-low latency (0.06ms) meets 8 KHz polling'. 0.06 ÷ 0.125 = 0.48. A figure shorter than the interval between USB reports cannot be an end-to-end latency. For scale, HLPlanet measured 0.60 ms wired on the sibling TK75 TMR, ten times that claim.
